reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not lighting/rigging practitioner approval
experience_basis: Current C1 course compared with MDQ-021–028, electrical and rigging evidence
findings: The course's support-vs-technical boundary is strong. Keep case/fixture/cable workflow conceptual and assigned. Any truss assembly, suspended-system interface or exact fixture-handling practice needs system/manufacturer and qualified-lead context before practical release.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not rigging practitioner approval
experience_basis: Current learner wording reconciled with OSHA 1926.1419 scope
findings: The phrase 'only STOP is universal' is too broad. OSHA requires stop/emergency-stop behavior in covered construction crane/derrick operations, but that does not establish one nationwide entertainment-rigging signal system. Later copy should teach: identify the designated caller/current system; if communication breaks down or a safety concern arises, stop/alert/escalate under the applicable procedure.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not electrical/legal approval
experience_basis: Current C1 electrical boundary compared with OSHA/ETCP power evidence
findings: Retain the hard boundary against treating C1 as electrical qualification. Avoid tying authority to a single job title such as Head Electrician because employer, jurisdiction and qualified-person rules can vary; use 'appropriately qualified/trained and assigned person' as the transferable formulation.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not audio/rigging practitioner approval
experience_basis: Current C1 course compared with MDQ-031–039 and current manufacturer/OSHA evidence
findings: Case/cable/department workflow and system-boundary teaching are appropriate. Product-specific cabinet/array handling, hardware and suspended-system interfaces need manufacturer and qualified practitioner context before becoming physical practice instruction.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not product/practitioner approval
experience_basis: Current course wording compared with current Neutrik documentation
findings: 'Do not force an abnormal connector' is a sound stop/ask rule. Exact insertion, locking, alignment, cleaning and inspection procedures must remain connector/model specific and should not be generalized from one XLR product family.

reviewer_name_or_role: AI-assisted evidence audit — not occupational-health approval
experience_basis: Current course compared with HR-08 OSHA noise correction
findings: Keep hearing protection site/exposure/program specific. Do not imply that every soundcheck automatically triggers one PPE rule or that OSHA action/permissible-exposure values are universal safe/unsafe boundaries.
